toolcolors 0.1.0
  • Reference

toolcolors — Implementation Plan

Color palettes and ggplot2 scales inspired by the album art of Tool. This document is the spec for implementing the package. Work through the steps in order; each step ends with something that can be checked.

0. Ground rules for the implementer

  • This is an existing usethis skeleton (DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE, R/, tests/testthat.R, README.qmd, GitHub Actions R-CMD-check). Build on it; do not regenerate it.
  • Document everything with roxygen2 (markdown enabled). Never hand-edit NAMESPACE or man/; run devtools::document().
  • Dependencies: ggplot2 in Imports; graphics and grDevices (base) in Imports too. testthat, knitr, vdiffr (optional) in Suggests. No other runtime dependencies.
  • Use base R for argument checking (match.arg(), stop(..., call. = FALSE)). Do not add rlang/cli just for messages.
  • Do not use the deprecated scale_name argument of ggplot2::discrete_scale() (deprecated in ggplot2 3.5.0).
  • Never commit or ship album artwork in the package (copyright). Cover images used for color extraction live only in data-raw/covers/, which is git-ignored and build-ignored.
  • All exported functions accept both color and colour spellings via aliases.

1. Housekeeping

  1. Update DESCRIPTION:
    • Title: Color Palettes Inspired by Tool Album Art
    • Description: Provides color palettes and 'ggplot2' color and fill scales inspired by the album artwork of the band Tool. Palettes can be used as discrete or interpolated continuous scales.
    • Imports: ggplot2 (>= 3.5.0), graphics, grDevices
    • Suggests: testthat (>= 3.0.0), knitr
    • URL: https://github.com/ekholme/toolcolors
    • BugReports: https://github.com/ekholme/toolcolors/issues
  2. Add to .Rbuildignore: ^data-raw$, ^PLAN\.md$, ^README\.qmd$ (already present).
  3. Add to .gitignore: data-raw/covers/.
  4. Add a disclaimer to README and package docs: “This package is not affiliated with or endorsed by Tool or the artists. Palettes are interpretations inspired by the artwork.”

2. The palettes

2.1 Important caveat about the hex codes

The hex codes below are a first draft derived from descriptions of the artwork, not eyedropped from the images. Before release, they must be refined with the extraction script in step 8 (run on covers the author supplies locally) and visually checked against the art. Keep the palette names, lengths, types and structure below stable; only the hex values should need tweaking.

2.2 Palette table

Each palette has: - colors — hex codes, listed in “natural” order (dark → light, or as they read in the art). This order is used for continuous scales. - order — a priority ranking of indices into colors. For a discrete palette of size n, use colors[order[seq_len(n)]]. The first few entries should be the most mutually distinct colors. - type — "sequential" or "qualitative"; informational, shown in docs and print(), and used to pick a sensible default in display_all().

name album (year) artwork notes type
opiate Opiate (1992) Grainy black-and-white/sepia photograph sequential
undertow Undertow (1993) Translucent ribcage sculpture; murky greens, bone, amber on black qualitative
aenima Ænima (1996) Cold blue lenticular figure; pale flesh; rust/flame accents in the packaging qualitative
lateralus Lateralus (2001) Alex Grey’s transparent anatomical figure: indigo, blue veins, gold, flame orange, crimson, magenta qualitative
ten_thousand_days 10,000 Days (2006) Alex Grey’s many-eyed figure: plum, oxblood, ochre-gold, olive, teal qualitative
fear_inoculum Fear Inoculum (2019) Eye-studded serpentine mandala: black, deep teal, turquoise, bronze, gold, rust qualitative

2.4 Album metadata

Also export a small data frame tool_albums (in R/palettes.R, not data/), one row per palette:

column example
palette "lateralus"
album "Lateralus"
year 2001L
type "qualitative"
n_colors 8L

n_colors and type must be computed from tool_palettes, not typed twice.

4. Core function: tool_palette() 

tool_palette(name, n, type = c("discrete", "continuous"), direction = 1)

Behavior: - name: one of names(tool_palettes). Unknown names error with a message listing valid names. - n: number of colors. Defaults to the palette length when missing. Must be a single positive whole number. - type = "discrete": - If n > length(colors), error: “Palette ‘x’ has only k colors; use type = "continuous" for more.” - Otherwise return colors[order[seq_len(n)]]. - type = "continuous": return grDevices::colorRampPalette(colors)(n) (natural order, not order). - direction: 1 or -1; -1 reverses the returned vector. Anything else errors. - Return a character vector with class c("tool_palette", "character") and attribute name set to the palette name. - Exported, with roxygen examples: tool_palette("lateralus"), tool_palette("aenima", 3), tool_palette("fear_inoculum", 50, type = "continuous").

5. print.tool_palette()

  • Draws the swatch in the active graphics device: graphics::image() of seq_along(x) with col = x, no axes, palette name as the title (graphics::rect() + text() is also fine).
  • Restores par() on exit (old <- par(mar = ...); on.exit(par(old))).
  • Invisibly returns x.
  • Registered as an S3 method (@export on the method in roxygen).

6. display_all() 

display_all(type = c("all", "sequential", "qualitative"))
  • Plots every matching palette stacked vertically in one device, labeled by name, each at its full length.
  • Restores par(); returns the palette names invisibly.

7. ggplot2 scales (R/scales.R)

Exported functions:

function aliases
scale_color_tool_d() scale_colour_tool_d()
scale_fill_tool_d() —
scale_color_tool_c() scale_colour_tool_c()
scale_fill_tool_c() —

Signatures:

scale_color_tool_d(palette = "lateralus", direction = 1, ...)
scale_color_tool_c(palette = "lateralus", direction = 1, ...)

... is passed to the underlying ggplot2 constructor (so name, labels, na.value, guide, etc. work).

Reference implementation (follow this pattern; it avoids the deprecated scale_name argument):

scale_color_tool_d <- function(palette = "lateralus", direction = 1, ...) {
  check_palette_name(palette)   # internal helper, errors early
  ggplot2::discrete_scale(
    aesthetics = "colour",
    palette = function(n) {
      unclass(tool_palette(palette, n = n, type = "discrete",
                           direction = direction))
    },
    ...
  )
}

scale_fill_tool_d <- function(palette = "lateralus", direction = 1, ...) {
  check_palette_name(palette)
  ggplot2::discrete_scale(
    aesthetics = "fill",
    palette = function(n) {
      unclass(tool_palette(palette, n = n, type = "discrete",
                           direction = direction))
    },
    ...
  )
}

scale_color_tool_c <- function(palette = "lateralus", direction = 1, ...) {
  cols <- unclass(tool_palette(palette, n = 256, type = "continuous",
                               direction = direction))
  ggplot2::scale_colour_gradientn(colours = cols, ...)
}

scale_fill_tool_c <- function(palette = "lateralus", direction = 1, ...) {
  cols <- unclass(tool_palette(palette, n = 256, type = "continuous",
                               direction = direction))
  ggplot2::scale_fill_gradientn(colours = cols, ...)
}

#' @rdname scale_color_tool_d
#' @export
scale_colour_tool_d <- scale_color_tool_d

#' @rdname scale_color_tool_c
#' @export
scale_colour_tool_c <- scale_color_tool_c

Document _d color + fill together on one help page (@rdname), and _c color + fill together on another. Each page gets a runnable example using a built-in dataset, e.g.

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy, color = class)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_color_tool_d("lateralus")

ggplot(faithfuld, aes(waiting, eruptions, fill = density)) +
  geom_raster() +
  scale_fill_tool_c("fear_inoculum")

Note: mpg$class has 7 levels — every palette must have ≥ 7 colors (all do) so the examples work for any palette.

8. Dev scripts in data-raw/ (not part of the package)

data-raw/extract_palette.R

Purpose: refine the hex codes from real cover images the author places in data-raw/covers/ (e.g. lateralus.jpg).

  • Uses magick (dev-only; do not add to DESCRIPTION).
  • Function extract_palette(path, k = 8, seed = 1):
    1. magick::image_read() → image_scale("200") to downsample.
    2. Convert to an RGB pixel matrix (as.integer(image_data(img, "rgb"))), reshape to an N x 3 matrix.
    3. Optionally convert to Lab (grDevices::convertColor(..., from = "sRGB", to = "Lab")) and run stats::kmeans(centers = k, nstart = 10) there.
    4. Return cluster centers as hex (via grDevices::rgb()), sorted by luminance, with cluster sizes, and draw a swatch.
  • At the bottom, loop over every image in covers/ and print results so the author can hand-pick colors (k-means finds dominant colors; small accent colors like Lateralus’ magenta may need a higher k or manual picking).

data-raw/check_palettes.R

  • For each palette, plot colorspace::swatchplot(cols, cvd = TRUE) (or colorblindcheck::palette_check(cols, plot = TRUE)) to see how it reads under deuteranopia/protanopia/tritanopia.
  • Report the minimum pairwise ΔE (Lab distance) among the first 3, 5, and 7 discrete colors. Use this to tune order so the first few colors are the most distinct.
  • Optional: add a colorblind_safe field to each palette later, based on this check.

9. Tests (tests/testthat/)

test-palettes.R - Every element of tool_palettes has colors, order, type. - All colors are valid 7-char hex (^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$). - order is a permutation of seq_along(colors). - type ∈ c("sequential", "qualitative"). - Every palette has ≥ 7 colors. - tool_albums has one row per palette and matching n_colors.

test-tool_palette.R - Default n returns full length. - Discrete n = 3 returns colors[order[1:3]]. - Discrete n > length errors with the “continuous” hint. - Continuous n = 100 returns 100 colors; first/last equal the palette’s first/last colors. - direction = -1 reverses output; direction = 2 errors. - Unknown name errors and the message contains a valid name. - Result has class tool_palette and name attribute. - print() returns invisibly (wrap in pdf(NULL) / dev.off()).

test-scales.R - Each scale function returns an object inheriting from "Scale". - Building a plot with scale_color_tool_d() on mpg + ggplot2::ggplot_build() yields colors that are all in the palette. - scale_fill_tool_c() builds without error on faithfuld. - scale_colour_tool_d is identical to scale_color_tool_d. - Invalid palette name errors at scale-construction time. - Discrete scale with more levels than colors errors on build.

One section per palette: swatch (print(tool_palette("x"))) + a small example plot (alternate scatter / bar / raster examples). 5. Usage examples for tool_palette(), discrete scales, continuous scales, direction = -1.

Render with devtools::build_readme(); commit generated figures in man/figures/.

  • devtools::document() produces no warnings.

  • README renders and shows every palette.
